scope: read-only timing derivation from retained owned native runs; no CEF launched by this audit

clock_basis.native: MonotonicNs: std::chrono::steady_clock converted to integer nanoseconds
clock_basis.basis: Trace and paint/consumer use the same MonotonicNs helper according to implementation history and native implementer review. The exact retained header matches the build; concurrent compile-only Goal changes prevent claiming byte-for-byte reproduction of the whole fixture source.

formulas.first_retained_paint_ms: (first retained frame.observed_ns - initialize_enter.observed_ns) / 1e6; not first actual callback or content-ready time
formulas.disk_consumer_ms: stored work-duration_ns / 1e6; includes file writes and lease release
formulas.p95: nearest-rank sorted sample at ceil(0.95*N), with N reported

checks: Strictly increasing frame indices/observation/acquisition timestamps; nonnegative frame age and duration.
Lifecycle phases unique and monotonic; derived intervals only within the native clock.
Frame sample count equals acquired count; no frames.json reports truncation.
First/latest retained metadata matches native sample index/time.
Paint/acquired/coalesced and callback counters checked without relabeling the residual as a specific drop reason.
All 100 lifecycle summary rows match report hashes and gates; eight initial BGRA files verified all-zero with matching raw/compressed hashes.

limits: FPS covers the active retained-sample interval and excludes startup/shutdown; it is a disk-consumer rate, not full-run delivered video FPS or 60-second benchmark acceptance.
First retained paint can be transparent and earlier callbacks may have coalesced; no content-ready or actual-first-paint claim.
max_callback_publish includes validation/locking/copy; individual callback timings and pure memcpy duration were not retained.
Disk consumer work includes first/latest writes and lease release, not an isolated transfer or native texture upload.
Accepted paint residuals may include pending/revoked work at close; no drop cause is fabricated.
Native shutdown intervals exclude process/helper exit; supervisor cleanup is a separate Python-clock observation.
Five-host frame timing is truncated startup (4/0/4/0/12 retained frames) and is unsuitable for scaling comparisons.
One-second fresh-process cycles do not establish long-lived-host leak freedom.
No cross-clock TTFF, GPU or libobs metric is derived.
